name: India's share of world manufacturing output (Bairoch)
method: Point values are Paul Bairoch's 1982 estimates for the territory of present India, Pakistan and Bangladesh, built by backward projection from per-capita industrial output and population. Bairoch gives no error bands; the low/high here are a +/-25% convention of this batch, wider in the pre-statistical 18th century, to signal how rough the numbers are.

name: Excess deaths in the Bengal famine of 1943-44
method: Central value: Dyson and Maharatna's 1991 re-estimate of excess mortality from registered deaths corrected for under-registration (about 2.1 million). Low: the Famine Inquiry Commission's 1945 figure (about 1.5 million). High: Sen's 1981 estimate of around 3 million.

name: Famine deaths in India, 1876-79
method: Low and high are the range Mike Davis compiles from contemporary and later demographic estimates for India in 1876-79 (6.1 to 10.3 million); the central value is simply the midpoint, not an estimate of its own.

name: Population of Greater Angkor at its peak
method: Klassen, Carter and Evans (2021) model population from lidar-mapped occupation mounds, residential ponds and temples, dated by archaeology, and give a peak of 700,000-900,000 for the Greater Angkor Region in the 13th century; the central value is the midpoint, and the year marks the 13th century, not a census year.
